amanda (support): FYI—Acme reporting intermittent stream resets to private inference endpoint behind NLB. Seen during heavy batch uploads (~5-20 req/s). Ticket #12345. Root cause suspect firewall/NACL. Attached traces.

carla (eng-sre): Steps to repro?

amanda (support): Repro steps customer provided:
1) pod -> `curl --http2 -v https://inference.private.acme:443/api/v1/stream -d @big.json`
2) handshake ok, then RST after ~30s when payload large/keepalive
3) tcpdump shows SYN/ACK from our side then client RST with src port 58001
Command they ran: `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 tcp and host 10.0.4.12 and port 443 -w /tmp/cap.pcap`
They also ran `curl -v --http2 --limit-rate 500k` which made it less frequent.

raj (infra): Could be asymmetric return path due to customer NACL blocking >61000 ephemeral ports. Ask them to check their NACL and on-prem firewall NAT port range.

tim (customer-success): I already asked them; they say NACL allows 1024-61000. Their NAT appliance assigns high ephemeral >61000 during concurrent connections.

carla (eng-sre): That would cause backend to send packets to src ports >61000, then customer NACL drops the return packets -> TCP tear down. Quick check: ask them to `sudo cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range` and show their NAT ephemeral range. Also request a pcap showing three-way handshake and where the RST originates.

amanda (support): Sent commands to customer:
```
# on client host:
cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range
sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 -w /tmp/pcap.pcap host 10.0.5.20 and port 443
curl -v --http2 https://inference.private.acme/api/v1/generate -d @1MB.json
```
They returned `32768 60999` and a pcap where our server sends SSE frames and then client RST for ports 61123, 61211, etc.

raj (infra): Ok that's the mismatch. Workarounds: 1) customer widen NACL to 1024-65535, 2) set their NAT to allocate <=60999 ephemeral, or 3) we can enable active connection draining/keepalive tuning (short-term mitigate). Recommend #1.

infra-bot: Logged support ticket 12345 -> infra-escalation, assigned to @carla.

carla (eng-sre): I'll draft KB note for future customers about ephemeral port ceilings causing asymmetric return path. Amanda, confirm if customer will change NACL; if not we'll ship keepalive tweak.

amanda (support): Customer agreed to widen NACL to 1024-65535. I'll close once they confirm test passes. :thumbsup:
